questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Extremely difficult. As a Nordic at NTNU you have to figure out housing completely at your own. Difficult due to the fact that most housing is only available for at least a 1 year period, and there are many exchange student in the autumn semester.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: NEVR2010 Introduction to Neuroscience (15 ECTS), TMA4195 Mathematical Modelling (7.5 ECTS), TMA4205 Numerical Linear Algebra (7.5 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The curriculum in NEVR2010 Introduction to Neuroscience (15 ECTS) is interesting and does not require any background in medicine, chemistry or biology. It's a very easy course considering it's 15 ECTS and it is taught 100% remotely. I do NOT recommend TMA4195 Mathematical Modelling. TMA4205 Numerical Linear Algebra is a great course with a great professor, great assignments and great curriculum. Very structured and thought out. Possible to take despite not meeting the many prerequisites, but it is not easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many norwegians rarely turn off the lights...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Every Wednesday on campus is "kanelbolleonsdag" and the entire campus smells of cinnamon rolls and coffee.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Norwegian is harder than anticipated because of the many dialects, and you will probably hang out much more with other exchange students than with Norwegians, so perhaps prioritise living with a bunch of Norwegians if you can. Nature is amazing and abundant there, but to go to the national parks you probably will need a car, so either bring one or rent on on e.g. Hyre. Going there either semester is probably equally amazing because of course summer is great but on the other hand it is not so dark in winter and so much fun stuff can be done in snow.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Møllenberg is a cool place to live.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going on weekend hiking- and roadtrips with awesome exchange students that I met there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That there is no vacation at all during the autumn semester.
